story: Outside AI money in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, with the Air Force AI data center lease offer and the uncounted Sullivan and Peltola race as context

claims.claim: An FEC analysis published by the Alaska Beacon found that Alaska's U.S. Senate race drew more money from AI company employees than any other 2026 Senate race.
claims.value: more than any other 2026 Senate race
claims.verbatim: Alaska’s U.S. Senate race has drawn more money to campaigns from employees of AI companies than any other 2026 Senate race
claims.notes: The article URL returns 403. Its text was read via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/ (offset 300000, pubDate Tue 03 Nov 2026 20:00:30 +0000, byline Arshya Gaur and Bridget Stuebner). The verbatim excerpt is cut at the extraction tool's limit, and its apostrophe is curly on the page. needs_softening true. This is the Beacon's own analysis, so write 'according to an Alaska Beacon analysis of FEC records'. AI companies are defined narrowly (see C21).

claims.claim: At least 19 AI company employees gave to the campaigns of Sen. Dan Sullivan and challenger Mary Peltola, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: The actual numbers of donors are small, but at least 19 employees contributed approximately $119,000
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The sentence goes on 'to the campaigns of Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and his Democratic challenger, Mary Peltola'. Say 'at least 19'.

claims.claim: Those AI company employees gave about $119,000 to the Sullivan and Peltola campaigns combined, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: at least 19 employees contributed approximately $119,000
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. Sanity check: $56,000 to Peltola (C07) plus $63,000 to the Sullivan campaign (C09) is $119,000. So the $119,000 leaves out the $35,000 to True North PAC (C10). needs_softening true. Write 'about $119,000'. The figure includes money routed through joint fundraising committees (C22 to C24), so it isn't all candidate-committee money.

claims.claim: Most of those donors gave close to the maximum legal contribution, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: with most people giving close to the maximum legal contribution limit.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. This is the end of the same sentence as C02 and C03.

claims.claim: Many of the donations to both candidates came from employees of Anthropic, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Many of the donations to both candidates came from employees of Anthropic, one of the country’s leading AI companies.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The FEC partly corroborates this (C34 to C36). Anthropic is the AI company that makes Claude, so a disclosure may be warranted if the deck's own tooling is involved.

claims.claim: None of the AI company donors listed an Alaska address, and most live in California, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: None of the AI-company donors list an Alaska address, with most living in California.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed.

claims.claim: Peltola received at least $56,000 from AI company employees, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: In the Alaska races, Peltola received at least $56,000
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. On the page the sentence continues after an em dash, which is excluded here. FEC cross-check: the OpenFEC employer aggregation for Alaskans for Mary (C00933978) shows only $3,500 from 'ANTHROPIC' (C36). That fits the Beacon's statement that more than half came through the Fish Family Freedom Fund (C24). needs_softening true. Write 'at least $56,000, much of it through a joint fundraising committee, according to the Beacon'.

claims.claim: Nearly all of Peltola's AI employee money came from Anthropic employees, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: nearly all of it from Anthropic employees.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. This is the second half of the C07 sentence.

claims.claim: Sullivan's campaign received about $63,000 from AI company employees, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Sullivan received approximately $63,000 from AI-company employees for his campaign.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. FEC partial cross-check: Alaskans for Dan Sullivan (C00570994) shows $35,000 across 13 receipts from donors listing Anthropic or Anthropic PBC as employer (C34, C35). OpenAI and xAI weren't queried, and JFC allocations may arrive later. The two figures aren't contradictory.

claims.claim: Another $35,000 from AI company employees went to Sullivan's leadership PAC, True North, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Another $35,000 came through his leadership PAC, True North, bringing his combined total to about $98,000.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The True North PAC committee wasn't queried on OpenFEC. Don't confuse it with the $35,000 Anthropic employer aggregate on the candidate committee (C34 plus C35). The two are equal by coincidence and are separate committees.

claims.claim: Sullivan's combined AI employee total, campaign plus leadership PAC, was about $98,000, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: bringing his combined total to about $98,000.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. Arithmetic checks ($63,000 plus $35,000 is $98,000). Don't add the $98,000 to Peltola's $56,000 and call it the race total. The article's race total is $119,000, which excludes the PAC.

claims.claim: Sullivan ranked fifth among Senate candidates nationwide in donations from AI company employees, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Sullivan alone was fifth out of other candidates for Senate races around the country in terms of donations received from AI company employees
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The extraction tool returned this sentence in two pieces, joined here. The page doesn't say whether the ranking uses the $63,000 or the $98,000 figure.

claims.claim: Peltola ranked 14th among Senate candidates nationwide in donations from AI company employees, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: from AI company employees and Peltola was 14th.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. This is the tail of the C12 sentence.

claims.claim: The top Senate candidate nationally for AI employee money was Republican Mike Rounds of South Dakota with $165,100, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: The top individual candidate is Republican Mike Rounds of South Dakota with $165,100 to his campaign and PACs
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The excerpt is cut at the tool's limit. Rounds's figure counts campaign plus PACs, which is comparable to Sullivan's $98,000 and not to his $63,000. Sanity check: Alaska tops races (C01) while Rounds tops individual candidates. Both hold because the Alaska race total combines two candidates.

claims.claim: A donor can give a federal candidate $3,500 per election, or $7,000 for the primary and general together, as the Beacon article states.
claims.verbatim: A donor can give $3,500 per election, or $7,000 for the primary and general together
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. Corroborated by the FEC primary source in C28. For the limit itself, cite C28.

claims.claim: A donor can also give $5,000 a year to a leadership PAC, as the Beacon article states.
claims.verbatim: and $5,000 a year to a leadership Political Action Committee or PAC.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The FEC contribution limits page lists '$5,000 per year' for an individual to a PAC (SSF and nonconnected). A leadership PAC is a nonconnected PAC, so the figure is consistent.

claims.claim: In the Beacon analysis Sullivan had the fewest AI employee donors but received the most per donor.
claims.verbatim: Sullivan had the fewest donors, but he received the most per donor.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. needs_softening true. The scouts' 'among the top 10' qualifier wasn't seen verbatim, so the comparison set is unconfirmed. Use it only as 'Sullivan had fewer donors giving more each, according to the Beacon', and don't add 'top 10'.

claims.claim: Counting Big Tech employees as well, Peltola's campaign ranks fifth among Senate candidates nationwide, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Peltola’s campaign ranks fifth among Senate candidates nationwide, compared with Sullivan’s 16th-place ranking.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The preceding clause reads 'When including contributions from employees at Google, Microsoft, Meta and other Big Tech firms,'. Keep this separate from the AI-only ranking (C12, C13), where Sullivan is fifth and Peltola 14th. The two fifth places are easy to confuse.

claims.claim: Counting Big Tech employees as well, Sullivan ranks 16th among Senate candidates nationwide, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: compared with Sullivan’s 16th-place ranking.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed.

claims.claim: Close to 150 Big Tech employees have given to Peltola compared with four for Sullivan, according to the Beacon analysis.
claims.verbatim: Peltola has received support from close to 150 Big Tech employees when compared with four for Sullivan.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The page says 'four', and the deck may render it as 4.

claims.claim: The Beacon analysis counted only Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI as AI companies.
claims.verbatim: For the analysis, Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI were counted as AI companies
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. This is a method caveat, and every AI-money figure depends on it.

claims.claim: Sullivan's AI employee contributions mainly came through One Team Senate Majority, a joint fundraising committee that splits money with the NRSC and other Republican campaigns.
claims.verbatim: contributions mainly came from One Team Senate Majority, which splits contributions among the National Republican Senatorial Committee and other Republicans’ campaigns
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The tool returned this in pieces, joined here. The sentence opens with 'Sullivan’s'.

claims.claim: Sullivan's AI employee contributions also came through his joint fundraising committee, Sullivan Victory.
claims.verbatim: and his joint fundraising committee, Sullivan Victory.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. Sullivan Victory is FEC committee C00609255 (see C29, C31).

claims.claim: More than half of Peltola's AI employee contributions came through the Fish Family Freedom Fund, which she formed in January with the Alaska Democratic Party and the DSCC.
claims.verbatim: More than half of Peltola’s contributions came from the Fish Family Freedom Fund, which she formed in January with the Alaska Democratic Party and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. The tool returned two pieces, joined here. The verbatim runs to about 31 words. This explains why the FEC direct view of Alaskans for Mary shows little Anthropic money (C36).

claims.claim: Brendan Fischer of the Campaign Legal Center told the Beacon that large contributions from a few employees in one industry can suggest donors see a candidate as favorable to their interests.
claims.verbatim: Large contributions from a small number of employees in the same industry can suggest that donors see a candidate as favorable to their interests, said Brendan Fischer, Director of Strategic Investigations at Campaign Legal Center.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. IMPORTANT. The tool reports that this passage is NOT inside quotation marks. It is reported speech, so the deck must paraphrase it with attribution and must not show it in quote marks as Fischer's words. Always pair it with his caveat (C26). The verbatim runs to about 36 words.

claims.claim: Fischer cautioned against using employer data as proof of coordinated giving, according to the Beacon.
claims.verbatim: However, he cautioned against using employer data as proof of coordinated giving.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed. This caveat balances C25, and the deck should not use C25 without it.

claims.claim: The Beacon story was reported by Stanford student journalists using DataTalk, a campaign finance AI agent built by Big Local News and the Stanford Open Virtual Assistant Lab.
claims.verbatim: reported this story with the DataTalk campaign finance AI agent developed by Big Local News and the Stanford Open Virtual Assistant Lab as part of a journalism class at Stanford.
claims.notes: Read via the Beacon feed, in three pieces joined here. The sentence opens 'Stanford student journalists Arshya Gaur and Bridget Stuebner'. This is a strong AI angle: an AI agent was used to report on AI money.

claims.claim: The FEC sets the 2025 to 2026 limit for an individual giving to a candidate committee at $3,500 per election.
claims.verbatim: $3,500* per election
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The section heading reads 'Contribution limits for 2025-2026 federal elections'. Footnote is '*Indexed for inflation in odd-numbered years.' The same page lists '$5,000 per year' for an individual to a PAC. The page carries no publication date, so date_of_source is the fetch date (background reference).

claims.claim: FEC records show Peter Corsell, listing Twenty First Century Utilities as employer, gave $7,000 to Sullivan Victory on May 1st.
claims.verbatim: CORSELL, PETER | TWENTY FIRST CENTURY UTILITIES | INVESTOR | MIAMI BEACH FL | 2026-05-01 | 7000.0 | SULLIVAN VICTORY C00609255
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This is the only result (count 1). The verbatim is the record's JSON field values joined with pipes. election_type is P. Filing image https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/fecimg/?202607159875391558. The date_of_source of July 15th is inferred from the image number (filing receipt date). Background-dated.

claims.claim: Alaskans for Dan Sullivan reported Corsell as the source of $3,500 for the primary and $3,500 for the general on May 1st, both entries labeled transfer memo.
claims.verbatim: CORSELL, PETER | TWENTY FIRST CENTURY UTILITIES | 2026-05-01 | 3500.0 | P2026 PRIMARY | TRANSFER MEMO ; 3500.0 | G2026 GENERAL | TRANSFER MEMO
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Two results (count 2). Images 202607159875814698 and 202607159875814683. The memo_text 'TRANSFER MEMO' means these are memo itemizations of money allocated to the campaign by a joint fundraising committee, not direct checks. ADVERSARIAL FLAG. Corsell's only Sullivan Victory receipt is $7,000 (C29), so these $7,000 of candidate-committee memo entries are most likely the same money allocated onward. If so, Corsell's traceable giving is $7,000, not $14,000, and The Alaska Current's table adds both columns (see C40, C37). This couldn't be proved without the Sullivan Victory transfer schedule. needs_softening true. The deck should say 'FEC filings show' and avoid summing the columns.

claims.claim: FEC records show Aaron Kapito, listing TFC Utilities as employer, gave $3,500 to Sullivan Victory on April 24th.
claims.verbatim: KAPITO, AARON | TFC UTILITIES | POWER | NEW YORK NY | 2026-04-24 | 3500.0 | SULLIVAN VICTORY C00609255
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This is the only result. Image 202607159875391575. election_type is P. The Alaska Current table also lists Kapito on April 24th as 'TFC partner'.

claims.claim: Alaskans for Dan Sullivan reported Kapito as the source of $3,500 for the primary on April 24th, labeled transfer memo.
claims.verbatim: KAPITO, AARON | TFC UTILITIES | POWER | 2026-04-24 | 3500.0 | P2026 | TRANSFER MEMO
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Image 202607159875814713. The same query also returns three entries for Robert S. Kapito of BlackRock. He is unrelated to TFC, so don't conflate the two. The same possible double count as C30 applies, since the Current's table lists Kapito at $3,500 plus $3,500.

claims.claim: Alaskans for Dan Sullivan reported Charles Hu, managing partner of Saige Consulting, as the source of $3,500 for the primary and $3,500 for the general on April 24th, labeled transfer memo.
claims.verbatim: HU, CHARLES | SAIGE CONSULTING | MANAGING PARTNER | BROOKLYN NY | 2026-04-24 | 3500.0 | P2026 | TRANSFER MEMO ; 3500.0 | G2026 | TRANSFER MEMO
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Images 202607159875814695 and 202607159875814681. The Alaska Current table dates Hu's gifts April 26th, but the FEC memo date is April 24th. Use the FEC date. Hu's Sullivan Victory receipts weren't queried (rate limit budget).

claims.claim: The OpenFEC employer aggregation for Alaskans for Dan Sullivan shows $28,000 from 10 contributions by donors listing Anthropic as employer in the 2026 cycle.
claims.verbatim: employer: ANTHROPIC | total: 28000.0 | count: 10 | committee_id: C00570994 | cycle: 2026
claims.notes: PRIMARY, live API query fetched November 7th. This is a PARTIAL, direct-committee view and never the article's total. It covers only the candidate committee and only the employer string. The aggregate may include JFC memo entries. Self-reported employer strings vary (see C35).

claims.claim: The same FEC aggregation shows a further $7,000 from 3 contributions by donors listing Anthropic PBC as employer to Alaskans for Dan Sullivan.
claims.verbatim: employer: ANTHROPIC PBC | total: 7000.0 | count: 3 | committee_id: C00570994 | cycle: 2026
claims.notes: PRIMARY, live API query. Together with C34, $35,000 across 13 receipts lists Anthropic on the candidate committee. That's a partial view and doesn't contradict the Beacon's $63,000 for all three AI firms.

claims.claim: The OpenFEC employer aggregation for Alaskans for Mary shows a single $3,500 contribution from a donor listing Anthropic as employer in the 2026 cycle.
claims.verbatim: employer: ANTHROPIC | total: 3500.0 | count: 1 | committee_id: C00933978 | cycle: 2026
claims.notes: PRIMARY, live query. This is a partial, direct-committee view only. The Fish Family Freedom Fund JFC wasn't queried. Consistent with the Beacon saying more than half of Peltola's AI money went through that JFC (C24). Don't present it as rebutting the $56,000.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that donors tied to Peter Corsell's network gave Sullivan's campaign and joint committee a combined $58,000.
claims.verbatim: bringing the total contributions from this network to $58,000.
claims.notes: Byline Lauren Windsor, headline 'EXCLUSIVE: Data center utility execs maxed out donations to Dan Sullivan'. The outlet is progressive-leaning. Its table totals $29,000 candidate plus $29,000 Sullivan Victory, and the rows sum correctly to $29,000 per column. needs_softening true. Write it only as 'according to The Alaska Current'. DISPUTED BY PRIMARY. FEC shows the candidate-committee entries as TRANSFER MEMO allocations (C30, C32, C33), which suggests the two columns may count the same money twice. The traceable FEC total could be about half. Prefer the FEC line items (C29 to C33) to this sum.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current's table lists seven donors tied to Twenty First Century Utilities, I Squared Capital and Saige Consulting.
claims.verbatim: 4/24 | Aaron Kapito | TFC partner | $3,500 | $3,500
claims.notes: The count was made from the article's table, which has 7 donor rows plus a TOTAL row. The rows are Kevin Crull (4/23), Aaron Kapito (4/24), Charles Hu (4/26), Ross Berger (4/28), Kenneth Hayes Nuss (4/29), Peter Corsell (5/1) and David Roux (5/15). The verbatim is one table row with its cells joined. needs_softening true. Write 'according to The Alaska Current'. Roux is tied only by 'a relationship with TFC per N. Slope docs', which is the weakest link.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that most of the network's donations came between April 23rd and May 1st, with another on May 15th.
claims.verbatim: the donations occurred between April 23 and May 1
claims.notes: The article also says 'Within a nine-day period last spring' and 'On May 15, another executive with ties to Corsell also contributed $3,500 to each committee'. The FEC dates checked (April 24th, May 1st) fall inside the range.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that Corsell contributed $14,000 in support of Sullivan's reelection.
claims.verbatim: All told, Corsell contributed $14,000 in support of Sullivan’s reelection bid.
claims.notes: needs_softening true. DISPUTED BY PRIMARY. FEC shows one $7,000 receipt at Sullivan Victory (C29) plus $7,000 of TRANSFER MEMO entries on the candidate committee (C30), which are probably the same money. Prefer 'FEC filings show Corsell gave $7,000 to Sullivan Victory, which reported allocating it to the campaign' and treat $14,000 as The Alaska Current's figure only.

claims.claim: According to The Alaska Current, TFC estimates North Slope Power at $13 billion for a basic build of up to 3 gigawatts.
claims.verbatim: TFC estimates a cost of $13 billion for a basic build of up to 3 gigawatts
claims.notes: needs_softening true. This is a developer projection reported second hand. Write 'TFC estimates, according to The Alaska Current'.

claims.claim: According to The Alaska Current, the North Slope Power cost rises above $27 billion with a southbound transmission line.
claims.verbatim: more than $27 billion with the addition of a southbound transmission line servicing more data centers
claims.notes: needs_softening true. This is a developer projection.

claims.claim: According to The Alaska Current, the North Slope Borough committed to an exclusive partnership with TFC through 2027 and $5 million for North Slope Power.
claims.verbatim: an exclusive partnership with the firm through 2027 and $5 million to advance North Slope Power.
claims.notes: needs_softening true. The Alaska Current says the commitment came in March. The Borough's own record wasn't fetched.

claims.claim: Sullivan's campaign and office didn't respond to The Alaska Current's requests for comment.
claims.verbatim: Neither Sen. Sullivan’s campaign nor office responded to multiple requests for comment.
claims.notes: This is a fairness note for any slide using C37 to C43.

claims.claim: The Air Force offered about 4,700 acres across Air Force and Space Force installations in Alaska for potential AI data centers.
claims.verbatim: build potentially a dozen data centers on 4,700 acres located across Air Force and Space Force installations in Alaska
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (outside the window). Byline Matthew Cox. The SAM.gov description is truncated and doesn't show the acreage. The AFCEC news page returned 403, so no primary was reached for this figure.

claims.claim: Twelve parcels were identified for potential data center development under the Air Force offer.
claims.verbatim: Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development
claims.notes: BACKGROUND.

claims.claim: The Air Force solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 covers AI data center development at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.verbatim: RFLP Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station
claims.notes: PRIMARY, from the SAM.gov record title. The issuing office is AF Installation and Mission Support Center, FA8903 772 ESS PK, JBSA Lackland TX. Background-dated (last modified July 15th).

claims.claim: The Air Force released its request for lease proposals for the Alaska AI data center sites on April 10th.
claims.verbatim: Along with releasing an April 10 request for lease proposal
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. SAM.gov's publishDate shows only the latest version (June 16th), not the original release.

claims.claim: The Air Force scheduled an industry day for the Alaska data center offer on April 23rd.
claims.verbatim: the service will host an April 23 industry day to discuss plans for building data centers across three Alaska installations
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The industry day was scheduled, and whether it was held wasn't confirmed. Coincidentally, it falls on the first day of the Current's donation window (C39). Don't imply a link.

claims.claim: Site visits were set for Elmendorf-Richardson on April 28th, Clear on April 29th and Eielson on April 30th.
claims.verbatim: site visits at Elmendorf Richardson on April 28, Clear on April 29, and Eielson on April 30
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, and these were scheduled visits.

claims.claim: Air and Space Forces Magazine reported in April that companies had until May 29th to submit proposals.
claims.verbatim: Companies have until May 29 to submit proposals.
claims.notes: CONFLICT RESOLVED as a timeline, not an error. May 29th was the original deadline as reported April 11th. The current SAM.gov version lists June 29th (C52), and the record has 10 modifications with a current version published June 16th. That's consistent with an extension, but the modification history wasn't fetched. Suggested phrasing is 'proposals were first due May 29th, and the SAM.gov record now lists June 29th'.

claims.claim: The SAM.gov record for AFCEC-26-R-0006 lists a response deadline of June 29th at 5 p.m. Eastern.
claims.verbatim: responseDateActual: 2026-06-29T17:00:00-04:00
claims.notes: PRIMARY. responseTimeZone is America/New_York. The current version publishDate is 2026-06-16T01:11:16+00:00.

claims.claim: The SAM.gov record for the Air Force AI data center solicitation is marked inactive.
claims.verbatim: isActive: false
claims.notes: PRIMARY, fetched November 7th. 'Inactive' means the posting is closed. It doesn't mean the offer was cancelled.

claims.claim: The SAM.gov record shows 10 modifications, the latest made July 15th.
claims.verbatim: modifiedDate: 2026-07-15T03:55:46+00:00 | modifications count: 10
claims.notes: PRIMARY. 03:55 UTC on July 15th is still July 14th in Alaska. 'July 15th' is the UTC date.

claims.claim: As of November 7th the SAM.gov record for the Air Force AI data center solicitation lists no awardee.
claims.verbatim: award: {"awardee":{"ueiSAM":null,"name":null}}
claims.notes: PRIMARY. A lease award might not post to SAM.gov at all, so the absence of a public award is shown here and isn't proof that no lease exists. needs_softening true. Write 'no award has been posted on SAM.gov'.

claims.claim: In unofficial results as of Wednesday afternoon, November 4th, Peltola had 48 percent of the U.S. Senate vote and Sullivan had 47.7 percent.
claims.verbatim: Peltola has 48% of the vote and Sullivan has 47.7%
claims.notes: Byline Mari Kanagy. These are first-round, unofficial, preliminary figures before ranked-choice tabulation, as of the Division of Elections release on Wednesday afternoon (November 4th). The Division of Elections site returned 503, so no primary was reached. The deck MUST say unofficial and give the timestamp. More counts are due November 9th or 10th, which may change this.

claims.claim: Peltola and Sullivan were separated by 637 votes in the unofficial count as of Wednesday afternoon, November 4th.
claims.verbatim: with the two front-runners separated by only 637 votes.
claims.notes: Corroborated independently by Alaska Public Media, November 6th, 5:35 PM AKST (Liz Ruskin), https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-11-06/peltola-campaign-demands-information-about-rejected-absentee-ballots , which reads 'Peltola currently leads Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan by about 600 votes in the U.S. Senate race.' Mark it unofficial.

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections had counted 215,912 ballots as of Wednesday afternoon, November 4th.
claims.verbatim: The Alaska Division of Elections has counted 215,912 ballots as of Wednesday afternoon
claims.notes: This is an unofficial count.

claims.claim: Roughly one quarter of all votes in Alaska had not been tallied as of the ADN's November 6th report.
claims.verbatim: roughly one-quarter of all votes have not been tallied
claims.notes: The ADN summary reports up to about 60,000 ballots outstanding, but that figure wasn't captured verbatim, so don't use it. Sanity check: 215,912 counted plus about 60,000 is about 276,000, and 60,000 is about 22 percent, which fits 'roughly one-quarter'.

claims.claim: Ranked choice tabulation for Alaska's general election is scheduled for November 18th.
claims.verbatim: On that day, ranked choice tabulation will also take place.
claims.notes: The preceding sentence names 'Nov. 18, the deadline for the final' overseas absentee ballots. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media, November 4th, 4:06 PM AKST, https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-11-04/6-takeaways-from-alaskas-election , which reads 'the state will still have to tabulate the ranked choices, which will happen on Nov. 18.'

claims.claim: November 25th is the state's target date to certify Alaska's election results.
claims.verbatim: Wednesday, Nov. 25: The target date for the state to certify election results.
claims.notes: This is a target date only. Write 'target'. ADN and Alaska Public Media both mention a federal lawsuit that seeks to block or halt certification if Sullivan loses. That wasn't captured verbatim, so it isn't a claim here. Certification could slip.

claims.claim: Two UAA associate professors wrote in an ADN op-ed that Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft of the University of Alaska's AI plan.
claims.verbatim: Anthropic’s Claude generated the initial draft, a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.notes: Authors are Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter, associate professors at the University of Alaska Anchorage. This is an OPINION piece and an ALLEGATION. needs_softening true. Write 'according to an op-ed by UAA professors Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter'. 'Concealed' is the authors' characterization, and the deck shouldn't adopt it as fact. Anthropic also appears in the lead story, so watch the framing.

claims.claim: The op-ed authors say Claude's role in drafting was not disclosed until October 9th.
claims.verbatim: a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.notes: needs_softening true. Attribute it to the op-ed. The disclosure document itself wasn't fetched (alaska.edu 503 per scouts).

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents commissioned a strategic document called AI Engaged in June 2026, according to the op-ed.
claims.verbatim: In June 2026, the board commissioned a strategic document called AI Engaged
claims.notes: Attribute it to the op-ed. The ADN news story of October 4th says Shier drafted the intent language 'over the summer at the request of regents' (C67), which is consistent.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents was scheduled to vote on the AI statement of intent on November 5th.
claims.verbatim: the University of Alaska Board of Regents will vote on Nov. 5
claims.notes: VOTE OUTCOME NOT FOUND. The op-ed predates the vote, the ADN education section shows no November 4th to 7th story on it, and alaska.edu was 503 for scouts. Say 'was scheduled to vote', and don't assert a result.

claims.claim: Of 150 UAA students cited for academic misconduct last semester, 119 used AI, the ADN reported.
claims.verbatim: Of the 150 students cited for academic misconduct, 119 used AI
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (outside the window). Byline Tim Rockey. ADN reports this as about 1.1 percent of UAA's more than 10,500 students. This is single-source news reporting of university data, and UA's own figures weren't reached.

claims.claim: The ADN reported that Shier drafted the University of Alaska's AI intent language over the summer at the request of regents.
claims.verbatim: Shier drafted the AI intent language over the summer at the request of regents.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. This ADN story doesn't mention Claude. The Claude claim rests only on the op-ed (C62).

claims.claim: An exchange agreement lets Enstar buy about 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas, with MEA and Hilcorp as the other parties.
claims.verbatim: allows Enstar to buy about 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas
claims.notes: Byline Ava White, published November 6th, 8:21 AM AKST. SINGLE SOURCE. The RCA order wasn't reachable (rca.alaska.gov 403s bots), and ADN business and the Enstar newsroom (404) produced nothing. Attribute it to Alaska Public Media. Use it in the docket only, with 'according to Alaska Public Media'. The three-party detail comes from the article's framing and isn't quoted verbatim.

claims.claim: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska approved the Enstar exchange agreement in late October, according to Alaska Public Media.
claims.verbatim: approved an exchange agreement in late October
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCE, and the primary RCA docket wasn't reachable. The exact approval date is unknown.

claims.claim: Enstar must deliver the equivalent amount of gas back to MEA by March 2028, according to Alaska Public Media.
claims.verbatim: Enstar has to deliver the equivalent amount of natural gas back to MEA by March 2028.
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCE.

claims.claim: Enstar aims to have between 6 and 7 billion cubic feet of gas in storage by the end of December, according to Alaska Public Media.
claims.verbatim: aims to have between 6 and 7 billion cubic feet of natural gas in storage by the end of December
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCE. This is a target. Per CLAUDE.md, the Gas Watch must not turn this into a shortfall verdict.

claims.claim: The exchange boosts Enstar's end of December storage projection to about 5 billion cubic feet, according to Alaska Public Media.
claims.verbatim: This agreement boosts projections to about 5 billion cubic feet.
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCE, and it's a projection. needs_softening true. Write 'projected'. Don't frame the difference from C71 as a predicted shortfall (Gas Watch rule).
